The old woman showed up shortly before the market closed.

Riko looked up and then looked away fast. She remembered her. Three days ago, this woman had bought one of the homemade charms that had been gathering dust in the corner of the cart, for two coppers. Now it hung around her neck, the thread fraying, the corners worn down.

A return, Riko thought. She didn't take returns. But for this one, maybe she would.

"Excuse me," the woman said. "The morning my grandson had a fever, I put this under his pillow."

"Okay."

"It went down."

Riko said nothing. That charm did nothing. Scrap paper, lint, and a spiral drawn on a whim. Nobody knew that better than the person who made it.

"It's a fake," her mouth said, on its own.

The woman smiled a little and wrapped the charm in both hands.

"I know. But it was real to me."

Then she set a single copper on the cart and turned away before Riko could say anything.

The charm's price was two coppers. The woman had left one. What the missing copper was supposed to pay for, Riko sat by the cart that night and wondered.
